Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 584 of 2022

Appellant :- Keshav Prasad Kushwaha And Another
Respondent :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Appellant :- Amit Kumar Srivastava,Ashok Kumar Pandey,Mamta Maurya,Piyush Tr

Counsel for Respondent :- Aditya Kumar Kushwaha,Alok Krishan Tripathi,G.A.
Hon'ble Nalin Kumar Srivastava,J.
(Ref:- Criminal Misc. Application No. 14 of 2024)
1. Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.

2. The present application on behalf of appellant No.1 Keshav Prasad Kushwaha has been moved with prayer to stay the execution of conviction and sentence awarded by Sessions Judge, Lalitpur vide judgement and order dated 17.01.2022 in S.T. No.263 of 2014, arising out of Case Crime No.
326 of 2014, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC I.P.C. and Section 4 Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Karari, District Kaushambi.
3.

Learned counsel for the applicant/appellant has submitted that in the aforesaid case, the learned Sessions Judge has recorded the conviction of appellant no.1 under Section 304B, 498A IPC and Section 4 Dowry Prohibition Act and he has been sentenced for maximum imprisonment for a Keshav Prasad Kushwaha And Another vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173360747/
1 period of seven years with fine of Rs.10,000/- along with default sentence.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the present appellant along with other appellant- Smt. Gyanmati has been granted bail by this Court vide order dated 19.04.2024 but however, no order to suspend the execution of the sentence has been passed by the court while passing the aforesaid bail order.
It is further submitted that the Criminal Appeal No. 584 of 2022 preferred against the impugned judgement and order has already been admitted by this Court.

It is further submitted that the applicant/appellant is working on the post of Roller Driver in Public Works Department and now department has issued a show cause notice dated 18.04.2024 to the appellant/applicant for absent from duty without notice.
The applicant submitted his reply on 24.05.2024 and according to the show cause notice he is neither suspended nor terminated from service.
The applicant has no other source of income for surviving his life with family except this service.
Therefore, suspension of execution of conviction and sentence is necessary so that he could continue in service on the post of Roller Driver, U.P. Public Works Department, Kaushambi.
It is further submitted that the present appellant has never been convicted previously in any case.
It is further submitted that due to the aforesaid reason, it is expedient in the interest of justice to suspend the execution of conviction and sentence passed in the impugned judgement.

4. Reliance has been placed upon the judgement of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of U.T.
Administration of Lakshadweep Vs. Mohd. Faizal and others 2023 0 Supreme (SC) 802 and Rahul Gandhi Vs. Purnesh Ishwarbhai Modi and another, 2023 0 Supreme (SC) 682.
5.

6. To proceed with the matter it would be apposite to go through the provisions of Section 389 Cr.P.C. which are relevant in the instant matter and the same is extracted as here-in-above:
"389. Suspension of sentence pending the appeal; release of appellant on bail.
(i) Pending any appeal by a convicted person, the Appellate Court may, for reasons to be recorded by it in writing, order that the execution of the sentence or order appealed against be suspended and, also, if he is in confinement, that he be released on bail, or on his own bond.

[Provided that the Appellate Court shall, before releasing on bail or on his own bond a convicted person who is convicted of an offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term of not less than ten years, shall give opportunity to the Public Prosecutor for showing cause in writing against such release:Provided further that in cases where a convicted person is released on bail it shall be open to the Public Prosecutor to file an application for the cancellation of the bail.
(2) The power conferred by this section on an Appellate Court may be exercised also by the High Court in the case of an appeal by a convicted person to a Court subordinate thereto.

Keshav Prasad Kushwaha And Another vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173360747/
2 (3) Where the convicted person satisfies the Court by which he is convicted that he intends to present an appeal, the Court shall,
(i) where such person, being on bail, is sentenced to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years; or (ii) where the offence of which such person has been convicted is bailable one, and he is on bail,
order that the convicted person be released on bail, unless there are special reasons for refusing bail,
for such period as will afford sufficient time to present the appeal and obtain the orders of the Appellate Court under sub-section (1); and the sentence of imprisonment shall, so long as he is so released on bail, be deemed to be suspended.

sentences.text:
(4) When the appellant is ultimately sentenced to imprisonment for a term or to imprisonment for life, the time during which he is so released shall be excluded in computing the term for which he is so sentenced."
7.

It reveals from the perusal of the provisions of Sub Section (1) of Section 389 Cr.P.C. that the appellate court is empowered to suspend the execution of the sentence or order appeal appealed against by recording in writing the reasons thereof.

Acting as an appellate court it may pass order for grant of bail to the appellant in case he is in custody in pursuance of a judgement of conviction but it is also to be clarified that to pass an order of suspension of the execution of the sentence or order appealed against is not necessary and automatic outcome of an order for grant of bail in an appeal.
Undoubtedly, non suspension of sentence may sometimes cause irretrievable injury to the appellant/convict further resulting into deep hardship to him.

8. Bhagwan Rama Shinde Gosai and others Vs. State of Gujarat, 1999 SCC (Cri) 553 is another authority wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court held that:-
"When a convict person is sentenced to a fixed period of sentence and when he files an appeal under any statutory right, suspension of sentence can be considered by the appellate court liberally unless there are exceptional circumstances. Of course, if there is any statutory restriction against suspension of sentence it is a different matter."
9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The legal dictum upon the issue in question in the instant matter has further been affirmed by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a recent judgement of Rahul Gandhi case (supra)
10.

So far as the present appeal is concerned, it was filed in the year 2022 and keeping in view the huge pendency of criminal appeals before this court one cannot certainly say as to at which point of time the instant criminal appeal would be decided.

11. In view of the aforesaid discussion and keeping in view the facts and circumstances of this case in entirety, this Court is of the view that keeping in view the larger mandate of the Article 14 & 21 of the Constitution of India it is a case wherein it is expedient in the interest of justice to pass an order for Keshav Prasad Kushwaha And Another vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173360747/
3 suspension of conviction and execution of the sentence during the pendency of the instant appeal.
12.

Accordingly, the application is allowed and execution of the impugned sentence and conviction is hereby suspended during the pendency of instant appeal in respect of applicant/appellant no.1 Keshav Prasad Kushwaha.
